messages.subject: Prediction for the response
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I am following the spde book and trying to predict the response with inla.posterior.sample(). However, I have some questions:

I have a covariate that relates to the cargo capacity of vessels and therefore it is somehow defined only for the locations I have. To make predictions I can only include this variable considering some value beforehand, for example, the medium value of the variable, right?
I have also the vessels as random effects. Since I, once more, do not know which vessels I have in the locations I want to predict, it doesn't make sense to include this random effect in the prediction, right?

I attach the code in order for you to see if I am doing this right.

Thank you in advance,
Lídia

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction for the response
parts:
Hi Lidia,

to verify that you have done it correct, you can always change the
observed data to something else and something you do know, and validate
the predictions there.

yes, if you're predicting a new location you'll need the covariates also
there (or use a model for those as well).

random effects, yes, they will have (likely) mean zero, but will
contribute to the prediction variance.

there is a nice tool in the function, inla.posterior.sample.eval()
which you can use both to extract variables from the simulation and
compute a new statistics. but your case it not to hard to do 'manually'.

All the best
H
